how-to-start-over-after-budget-failure.alt: A comparison of catching up on old spending versus starting from today's balance, beside a note that a budget only needs to be true from today.
how-to-start-over-after-budget-failure.caption: Two ways back to a budget you trust.

end-of-month-money-review.alt: A table showing that recurring income, bills and spending groups carry into next month while one-off spending does not, beside the five step ten minute review checklist.
end-of-month-money-review.caption: Recurring things return; one-off things stay with the month they happened in.

how-to-cancel-subscriptions.alt: A script of three lines to say when a company resists a cancellation, beside a checklist for confirming the subscription really ended.
how-to-cancel-subscriptions.caption: Keep it short and polite, and say the same thing again if you need to.

debt-snowball-vs-avalanche.alt: A table comparing snowball and avalanche on three debts: first debt cleared, debt-free month and interest paid, beside a card showing a $113.94 difference.
debt-snowball-vs-avalanche.caption: A worked example of three debts with $200 a month extra. Your numbers will differ.

monthly-bills-list.alt: A card showing eight bills added up to $1,891 a month, including three that are not billed monthly.
monthly-bills-list.caption: Example: $223 a month hides in the bills that are not monthly.

organize-your-finances-from-scratch.alt: A checklist of six money areas to write down from memory, with question marks for the gaps.
organize-your-finances-from-scratch.caption: Ten minutes, no statements needed. Mark every gap with a question mark.

split-bills-with-a-partner-or-roommate.alt: A card showing four shared bills and the two thirds share one partner pays, totaling $1,328 of $1,992.
split-bills-with-a-partner-or-roommate.caption: Example: $4,200 and $2,100 take-home gives a 67 and 33 percent split.

subscription-tracker-what-to-track.alt: A small tracker table listing three subscriptions with their renewal dates and a keep, cancel or deciding status.
subscription-tracker-what-to-track.caption: Example: the annual rows are the ones with a decision waiting.

bank-statement-csv-to-budget.alt: A four step timeline for turning a bank statement CSV into a budget, beside a note that a transaction list cannot show what is coming.
bank-statement-csv-to-budget.caption: Download, map, review, then categorize, with nothing counted until you have reviewed it.

financial-binder-what-to-include.alt: A table of confidence labels for a financial binder entry: confirmed, estimated, unresolved and stale, beside a note listing the seven sections.
financial-binder-what-to-include.caption: Marking how sure you are stops a binder becoming a source of false confidence.

sinking-funds-explained.alt: A table working out a monthly sinking fund amount of $112.50 from $600 needed, $150 saved and four months left, beside a checklist of costs worth saving for.
sinking-funds-explained.caption: Example figures: $600 needed by year end, $150 saved, four months left.

50-30-20-rule-where-it-breaks.alt: A table of the 50/30/20 rule splitting after-tax income into needs, wants and savings, beside a comparison of when it fits and when it breaks.
50-30-20-rule-where-it-breaks.caption: The rule as a starting point: test it against your own month.

budget-for-variable-bills.alt: A table showing a variable bill with a low of $60 and a high of $122, planning toward $122 and setting aside $62 in a low month, beside a checklist of bills that move.
budget-for-variable-bills.caption: An illustration only. Use your own twelve months.

credit-card-minimum-payments-how-long.alt: A table comparing three extra payment amounts on the same debts by debt-free date and interest, beside a card showing only $30 of a $90 minimum reduces the balance.
credit-card-minimum-payments-how-long.caption: Example: three debts starting September 2026, constant rates. A comparison, not a forecast.

why-productivity-tools-fail-at-life-admi.alt: A table comparing what task apps assume about work with how life admin actually behaves: connected, already remembered, interrupting, and overwhelming all at once.
why-productivity-tools-fail-at-life-admi.caption: Where a generic task app's assumptions and life admin's reality pull apart.

flight-changed-what-else-is-affected.alt: A two-column card of what a moved flight affects: transfer, hotel check-in and dinner booking, against what was booked before it, plus three questions to ask per booking.
flight-changed-what-else-is-affected.caption: When a flight moves, check what was booked after it. Nothing booked before it is affected.

flight-delayed-with-a-connection-what-to.alt: A timeline of the first twenty minutes after a delay, from checking the arrival time to knowing what you want at the desk, and a short script for the airline agent.
flight-delayed-with-a-connection-what-to.caption: The order of the first twenty minutes when a delay threatens a connection.

hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.alt: A three-line script for the hotel desk when the booking cannot be found, and a checklist of five ways to ask them to search for it.
hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.caption: An example opening for the desk. Change any of the words.

organising-a-multi-stop-trip-without-a-s.alt: A checklist of the four things to record per booking, and a note about writing down what each booking depends on.
organising-a-multi-stop-trip-without-a-s.caption: The four things to record for every booking on a trip with many stops.

travel-document-checklist.alt: A small table listing each traveler's passport with an expiry date beside the name, and the insurance card, one row per document.
travel-document-checklist.caption: Example: one row per document, with the expiry date beside the name.

how-to-plan-a-group-trip.alt: A table for a group of six listing each booking, who booked it, and which people are on it, including a dinner that one person skips.
how-to-plan-a-group-trip.caption: Example: each booking, who made it, and who is on it.

what-to-keep-on-paper-when-you-travel.alt: A short checklist of what goes on the one printed travel page: local-language address, booking references, insurance, a home contact, passport copies.
what-to-keep-on-paper-when-you-travel.caption: The five things on the page, before you print two copies.

how-to-write-a-one-page-trip-itinerary.alt: A short itinerary table with a time, place and confirmation reference on each line, for a flight, hotel, tram tour and train.
how-to-write-a-one-page-trip-itinerary.caption: Example: one line per booking, with the reference beside it.

packing-list-for-a-week-away.alt: A checklist of the five basics every trip needs, with a note about adding two or three extras for this particular trip.
packing-list-for-a-week-away.caption: The first layer of a packing list, before you add what this trip needs.

carry-on-only-packing-list.alt: A checklist of four ways to make a week fit in a carry-on, and a note on the order: bag, list, pack, weigh.
carry-on-only-packing-list.caption: Ways to make it fit, once the bag is chosen.

packing-and-planning-for-a-trip-with-kid.alt: A two-column comparison of travelling alone against travelling with a child or baby: packing, timing and plans, with a note on leaving gaps.
packing-and-planning-for-a-trip-with-kid.caption: What changes when children come along.

lost-passport-wallet-or-phone-abroad-wha.alt: A checklist of five things to have ready before calling about a lost passport, wallet or phone, and a note to tell one person first.
lost-passport-wallet-or-phone-abroad-wha.caption: What to gather before you make the first call.

first-international-trip-checklist.alt: A timeline of a first international trip from checking the passport to sorting payment, phone and insurance, with a note to check rules at the official source.
first-international-trip-checklist.caption: The order to sort a first trip abroad, from the day you decide.

road-trip-planning-checklist.alt: A blank planning page with five things to fix before a road trip, and a checklist of four things to keep in the car.
road-trip-planning-checklist.caption: The few decisions to make before you drive.

night-before-you-travel-checklist.alt: A checklist of night-before checks: ID, card and cash, booking copies, phone charged and tomorrow's times, with a note about the house.
night-before-you-travel-checklist.caption: The night-before list. Six checks in all, the sixth is the house.

what-is-due-on-my-car-right-now.alt: A table of four car jobs with miles and months since each was done, showing which limit decides and one job with no date.
what-is-due-on-my-car-right-now.caption: An example with made-up numbers. Miles or months, whichever comes first.

what-to-tell-a-mechanic-before-work-star.alt: A card with three lines to say at a repair shop: the job you are requesting, a spending limit and a request for written prices.
what-to-tell-a-mechanic-before-work-star.caption: Three sentences to say before the keys change hands. The amounts are examples.

used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.alt: A five-item checklist for the first week with a used car that has no service records, from asking the seller to starting a log.
used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.caption: Five steps for a car that came with no paperwork.

car-maintenance-log-what-to-write-down.alt: A sample car maintenance log with three lines, each showing a date, an odometer reading in miles and the work done.
car-maintenance-log-what-to-write-down.caption: An example log. Date, miles and what was done on every line.

selling-your-car-with-a-service-history.alt: A blank service record page with fields for date, miles, what was done, who did it and notes, beside a note to include only what you can back up.
selling-your-car-with-a-service-history.caption: The shape of a record to print for a buyer. Keep receipts separately.

car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-yo.alt: A blank three-row table with job, miles and months columns to fill in from the owner's manual, and a note about harder driving conditions.
car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-yo.caption: A page to copy your manual's intervals onto, once. Leave a column blank if the manual does.

winter-car-prep-checklist.alt: A winter car checklist covering battery, tires, wiper blades, washer fluid and lights, with a note to check the emergency kit is complete.
winter-car-prep-checklist.caption: Five checks plus the emergency kit. Note the date, even if nothing needed doing.

two-cars-one-household-maintenance.alt: A blank one-page record for a single car with name or plate, job, miles, insurance and registration dates, and a note to review both cars monthly.
two-cars-one-household-maintenance.caption: Keep each car's record on its own page, and check both together.

glove-box-checklist-what-to-keep.alt: Two checklist cards, one listing what to keep in a glove box such as registration and proof of insurance, and one listing what to leave at home.
glove-box-checklist-what-to-keep.caption: Keep the details in the car and the originals at home.

car-paperwork-dates-organizer.alt: A small table of car registration and insurance dates with an act-by date six weeks earlier, and a note to look six weeks ahead once a month.
car-paperwork-dates-organizer.caption: An example tracker with made-up dates.

first-car-checklist-for-new-drivers.alt: A timeline of the first week with a new car, from calling the insurer to setting up the glove box, and a note to match the VIN in three places.
first-car-checklist-for-new-drivers.caption: The order that keeps the hard-to-fix things first.

life-admin-the-work-nobody-teaches-you.alt: A short checklist of what life admin work needs: somewhere for details, how they connect, a quick answer to what's due, help at the moment, and quiet when there's none.
life-admin-the-work-nobody-teaches-you.caption: What this kind of work actually needs, whatever you use to track it.
